title: Evaluate and roll out cross-encoder variants for reranking with multilingual and latency SLAs
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Goal: select and deploy a cross-encoder reranking model family that meets our multilingual quality targets while keeping 95th-percentile latency below the rerank SLO (30ms per query at 8k qps target) for the hosted API. Scope includes benchmark suite expansion, CI regression checks, quantized/float variants evaluation, and a staged rollback-safe rollout plan.

Context: current bidirectional+dot-product rerank pipeline (dual-encoder + lightweight scorer) has good throughput but shows quality regressions on long-tail multilingual queries and named-entity-heavy search logs. Prior internal experiments (ENG-4512) validated cross-encoders improve MAP@10 on many datasets but were not production-ready due to latency and scaling gaps. This ticket operationalizes model selection and delivery for production rerank endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark suite covers EN, ES, DE, FR, ZH with curated and sampled production prompts
Selected cross-encoder variant demonstrates >=5% relative MAP@10 improvement on multilanguage evals vs baseline AND 95th-pct latency <=30ms at target QPS on dedicated serving config
Quantized (8-bit) variant evaluated with <2% quality drop vs FP16 and <20% throughput regression
CI includes automated rerank regression checks that fail PRs with >1.5% drop on anchor prompt set
Runbook and rollback playbook documented; canary rollout plan defined and validated in staging
tasks: Expand multilingual eval harness: add ES/DE/FR/ZH datasets and sampled production queries (Sofia to lead)
Train/finetune candidate cross-encoder checkpoints: baseline-large, distilled-medium, multilingual-adapter (Research)
Build perf harness that measures p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU utilization at ramping QPS (Infra)
Evaluate INT8 and 8-bit quantized kernels on dedicated workers (Runtime)
Integrate regression guard into CI: nightly runs + PR check that compares to anchor baseline (Developer Experience)
Design staged rollout: staging canary -> 5% prod -> 25% prod -> 100% with automated rollback criteria
Create dashboard in Console for per-model rerank quality and latency by locale
Author runbook and incident playbook for rerank regressions and memory/oom events
benchmark_summary: Initial offline runs (2026-02-28): baseline dual-encoder MAP@10 averaged 0.412 across EN/ES/DE/FR. Candidate cross-encoder-large (FP16) achieved 0.456 (+10.7%). Distilled-medium achieved 0.438 (+6.3%) with 40% lower GPU memory. Throughput estimates on a p4d-like instance: cross-encoder-large FP16 p95=78ms at 2k qps; distilled-medium p95=34ms at 4k qps. INT8 quantization reduced p95 by 18% on distilled-medium but introduced a 1.9% MAP drop. These guided the selection of distilled-medium-quantized as primary candidate for canary.
decision_log: 2026-03-02 - Decided to prioritize a distilled multilingual cross-encoder variant for canary due to better latency/quality tradeoff and lower memory footprint (decision made by Ethan, Ava, Priya)
2026-03-05 - Agreed to require automated regression gates in CI before any model PR is merged (PM: Lucas approved)
2026-03-08 - Selected quantized INT8 as supported production variant provided nightly parity checks show <2% quality delta
implementation_notes: Serving mode: run cross-encoder on dedicated low-latency pool with continuous batching disabled for tail latency, small dynamic micro-batches for cost-efficiency. Use K/V cache for prefix scoring where applicable. Kernel notes: enable fused attention kernels for sequence length <=128, fallback to generic for longer. Memory: pin distilled-medium to single GPU worker to avoid cross-GPU syncing overhead. Add 'rerank.model_variant' metadata to request traces for per-variant attribution.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: p95 latency spikes under bursty traffic -> Mitigation: implement autoscale headroom and enable region fallback to nearest compatible variant
Risk: INT8 quality regressions on low-resource languages -> Mitigation: nightly lang-specific checks and automatic routing to FP16 variant for failing locales
Risk: Increased cost per token -> Mitigation: enable adaptive rerank where only top-K candidates from dual-encoder are sent to cross-encoder and experiment with K per locale
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Staging validation with synthetic traffic and 10K sampled production queries (complete)
Stage 1: Canary at 2% traffic for 72h, monitor latency, error rates, and MAP@10 on live-sampled evals
Stage 2: Expand to 20% for 48h if canary metrics stable; run full cost delta analysis
Stage 3: 100% with gradual traffic ramp and 7-day burn-in monitoring
Rollback criteria: >2% drop in MAP@10 on anchor set, >10% increase in p95 latency, or error rate >0.5% absolute
ci_and_tests: Added nightly 'rerank-regress' job that runs selected anchor prompt set across locales and compares to baseline metric artifacts stored in artifact store. PRs that change model weights or scoring code must include a CI artifact with baseline vs candidate metrics. Alerts created in PagerDuty on nightly regression failure.
